K2SymbolsBrauer.summary: Nothing K-theoretic in this roadmap exists: neither library has a Steinberg group, K₁ or K₂ of a ring, Milnor K-theory, Steinberg, tame or Dennis–Stein symbols, Weil reciprocity, a Hilbert symbol or a local invariant map, and Tau Ceti's algebraic K-theory stops at K₀. The substrate to consume is substantial: Tau Ceti's commutator relations and diagonal decompositions for elementary matrices over any commutative ring, its H² classification of extensions, Mathlib's group homology, unit parts and residues for discrete valuations, degree-one norm formulas for ideals, Tau Ceti's function-field places with residues, norm residues, divisor evaluation and disjoint-support moving (the apparatus for Weil reciprocity) with places matched to primes of affine models, and for T.7 the Kummer map, a (1,1) cup product and Mathlib's étale sheaf cohomology. Genuinely missing is every stated theorem: St(A) and its universal central extension, K₂ ≅ H₂(E(A)) and the homotopy comparison, Matsumoto, the tame symbol and localisation comparison, Bass–Tate, Milnor transfers and Weil reciprocity, the tame kernel with K₂(ℤ), K₂(F_q) and K₂(ℚ), Dennis–Stein presentations, and the Galois-symbol, Tate, Hilbert-symbol and reciprocity comparisons.

targets.target: Steinberg group St_n(A) presented by generators x_ij(a) and the Steinberg relations, with distinct-index hypotheses explicit
targets.note: Neither library has a Steinberg group of a ring. Mathlib has no occurrence of 'Steinberg'. Every Tau Ceti 'Steinberg' declaration is a Frobenius or graph-twisted Steinberg endomorphism of a group of Lie type (CFSG files), the Steinberg representation of GL₂(F_q), or the quaternion Steinberg relation, as the layer itself warns. Mathlib's `PresentedGroup` could carry the presentation. Tau Ceti proves that the relations hold for transvections in GL_n(A) for commutative A (`commutatorElement_transvectionUnit`), which is what the map St_n(A) → GL_n(A) would need.

targets.target: Stabilisation maps St_n(A) → St_{n+1}(A) and the stable Steinberg group St(A)
targets.note: No colimit of Steinberg groups, and no colimit of the GL_n tower either. Mathlib's `DirectLimit` of groups is the generic tool.

targets.target: The surjection St(A) ↠ E(A) sending x_ij(a) to the elementary matrix e_ij(a)
targets.note: Elementary matrices exist in GL_n(A) for commutative A (`Matrix.GeneralLinearGroup.transvection`, Tau Ceti's `transvectionUnit`), but neither the stable elementary group E(A) nor any map out of a Steinberg group exists.

targets.target: Centrality of the kernel of St(A) → E(A) in the stable range
targets.note: Absent with the Steinberg group; the layer's separate finite-rank caveat has nothing to attach to either.

targets.target: Universal-central-extension property of St(A) → E(A)
targets.note: Mathlib has `GroupExtension` with no centrality predicate. Tau Ceti classifies extensions with abelian kernel up to equivalence by the H² class of their factor sets (`GroupExtension.nonempty_equiv_iff_cohomologyClass_factorSet_eq`, with factor sets modulo coboundaries in `FactorSet.cohomologyClassEquiv`), and extensions built from trivial-action factor sets are central (`FactorSet.inl_range_le_center`). Neither library defines a universal central extension or proves that a perfect group has one.

targets.target: Classical K₂(A) defined as the kernel of St(A) → E(A)
targets.note: Neither library has K₂ of a ring in any form: Tau Ceti's algebraic K-theory stops at K₀ (split, exact, abelian and triangulated Grothendieck groups, and K₀ of finitely generated projectives).

targets.target: K₂(A) ≅ H₂(E(A), ℤ) via the universal central extension
targets.note: Mathlib has group homology in all degrees with `groupHomology.H2` and H₁ ≅ abelianisation (`H1AddEquivOfIsTrivial`), so H₂(G, ℤ) can be formed for any group G. There is no Hopf formula, no computation of H₂ of a perfect group, and neither E(A) nor K₂(A).

What exists is general infrastructure: Mathlib's group homology by the bar complex with explicit degree-3 chains, differentials and chain maps, the Tor functor, roots of unity, tensor and exterior powers over ℤ (with Tau Ceti's antisymmetric tensors), spectral sequences, the doubly transitive action of GL on projective space and the invariants r₁ and r₂. Genuinely missing is all of V.1–V.6, from K₃(A) ≅ H₃(St(A), ℤ) through the Bloch-group conventions and Suslin's theorem to K₃(F_q), K₃(ℤ) ≅ ℤ/48 and K₃(ℚ(i)), Bloch-element certificates and the regulator comparisons.

targets.note: Neither library has the plus construction, a classifying space BG of a discrete group, a K-theory space, or connected covers beyond the universal cover. KTheoryFiniteLocalFields.summary: Almost none of this roadmap exists: neither library has K_n of a ring for n ≥ 1, finite-coefficient K-theory or Bockstein sequences, rigidity, topological K-theory or Bott periodicity, Brauer lifting or Adams operations, Hochschild, THH, TR or TC, de Rham–Witt complexes, Hilbert symbols, local Tate duality, or Tate twists ℤ_p(j). Already built are K₀(F_q) = ℤ, which Tau Ceti proves for every division ring by dimension, and the Witt-vector algebra L.5 consumes (Mathlib), and the degree-one determinant has its finite-rank inputs (SL_n = E_n over fields, det surjective). The arithmetic to consume includes henselian pairs and the henselian instances for local rings of integers and adic completions, μ_n(R) ≅ μ_n(k), the Teichmüller identification μ_{q−1} ≅ k^× with the unit filtration, completions at finite places as local fields, |GL_n(F_q)|, Frobenius and norms of finite fields, Kähler differentials, continuous cohomology, the Kummer map and the cyclotomic character. Genuinely missing: Quillen's calculation, rigidity, Moore's theorem for K₂ of local fields, the trace calculations, the local higher K-groups and every local-to-global compatibility.

targets.note: `TauCeti.SplitK0.finrankEquiv : SplitK0 (FGModuleCat k) ≃+ ℤ` holds for every division ring k by dimension (with a smallness hypothesis that every finite field satisfies), so in particular for F_q. The abelian K₀ version is `AbelianK0.finrankEquiv`.

targets.note: Neither library has K_n of a ring for n ≥ 1, with or without coefficients; Tau Ceti's algebraic K-theory stops at K₀. Mathlib knows |GL_n(F_q)| (`Matrix.card_GL_field`), which the layer says is not enough.

targets.note: Group (co)homology exists for any group, but there is no homological stability and no computation for GL_n(F_q).

targets.note: `grep -rn -i` for Brauer lifting finds nothing; the Brauer group of a field in both libraries is unrelated.

targets.note: No Adams operations, homotopy fibres of spaces (Mathlib's homotopy fibre is for chain complexes) or plus construction. The Frobenius-side ingredients are field-theoretic: the Frobenius automorphism generating Gal(F_{q^n}/F_q) (`FiniteField.frobeniusAlgEquivOfAlgebraic`), and Tau Ceti's Frobenius-fixed subfields of a separably closed field of characteristic p, of order p^n (`frobeniusFixedSubfield`, `card_frobeniusFixedSubfield`).

targets.note: Mathlib has topological vector bundles, but no monoid of their isomorphism classes, no KU and no Bott periodicity. Tau Ceti's `realCliffordBottEquiv` is the algebraic periodicity of real Clifford algebras, not topological Bott periodicity.

targets.target: Restriction and transfer for finite extensions of finite fields in the functorial model, with formulas independent of any choice of cyclic generator
targets.note: Absent. Only degree-one field arithmetic exists, for example surjectivity of the norm between finite fields (`FiniteField.norm_surjective`).

targets.note: Degree one has its finite-rank inputs: SL_n(K) is generated by elementary transvections over any field (Tau Ceti `closure_range_toSpecialLinearGroup_eq_top_of_field`) and the determinant GL_n → units is surjective (Mathlib `det_surjective`), which together give GL_n(F_q)/E_n(F_q) ≅ F_qˣ at each rank, although no declaration states it. KTheoryLowDegrees.summary: Tau Ceti already has the degree-zero foundation: K₀ of finitely generated projectives over any ring as the exact K₀ of a split exact structure, with its universal property, the Cartan map to G₀ and the resolution theorem, K₀ ≅ ℤ for division rings, and K₀ ≅ G₀ with a basis of simple classes for semisimple rings. Mathlib supplies projectives as retracts of Rⁿ, the locally constant rank on Spec with base change, freeness over local rings, and Pic with Cl ≃ Pic and rank-one Steinitz, and Tau Ceti adds Cl(𝒪_S) ≅ Cl/⟨S⟩ and E(F) as the degree-zero divisor class group. For K₁ there are only finite-rank matrix inputs over commutative rings: elementary matrices with their commutator relations, SL_n = E_n over fields and over ℤ, the diagonal decomposition behind Whitehead's lemma, and units of a free extension as matrices whose determinant is the norm. Genuinely missing: GL(A), E(A) and K₁ with Whitehead's lemma for general rings, the stable determinant, SK₁ and Bass–Milnor–Serre, the S-unit rank formula, relative K₁, λ-operations and det: K₀ → Pic, Steinitz in rank ≥ 2 and K₀ ≅ ℤ ⊕ Pic, K₀ of schemes and curves, the product and projective-bundle formulas, and every comparison with higher K-theory.

targets.target: GL(A) as the filtered colimit of the GL_n(A) along g ↦ diag(g,1), with finite representatives and equality after a common stabilisation
targets.note: Mathlib's `DirectLimit` of a directed system of groups carries a group structure (its instance is in `Mathlib/Algebra/Colimit/DirectLimit.lean`), and Mathlib extends an elementary matrix e to the block matrix diag(e, 1) (`TransvectionStruct.toMatrix_sumInl`), but neither library builds the stabilisation embedding GL_n(A) → GL_{n+1}(A) or the colimit of the tower.

targets.target: Block sums and the elementary matrices e_ij(a) in the actual general linear groups
targets.note: The elementary matrices exist in GL over a commutative ring (Mathlib's `Matrix.GeneralLinearGroup.transvection`, Tau Ceti's `TauCeti.transvectionUnit`; Mathlib's `Matrix.transvection` itself assumes a commutative ring). Block sums exist as ring homomorphisms on matrices and endomorphisms (`Matrix.blockDiagonal'RingHom`, `LinearMap.prodMapRingHom`) and as Tau Ceti's unbundled `LinearMap.GeneralLinearGroup.prodMap` on GL(V) × GL(W) → GL(V × W). Missing: the block-sum homomorphism GL_m(A) × GL_n(A) → GL_{m+n}(A), and elementary matrices over a noncommutative ring, which the layer's general A requires.

targets.target: The stable elementary subgroup E(A)
targets.note: No elementary subgroup E_n(A) of GL_n(A) is named for a general ring, and there is no stable version. Tau Ceti's `transvectionUnit_mem_of_adjacent` shows that a subgroup of GL_{m+1}(A) containing the adjacent transvections contains all of them. The elementary subgroups in Tau Ceti's Lie-theory files belong to Chevalley groups, not to GL_n of a ring.

targets.target: Elementary commutator identities [e_ij(a), e_jl(b)] = e_il(ab) and the commuting cases
targets.note: Tau Ceti proves these in GL_n(A) and in SL_n(A) for distinct indices i, j, l, with explicit index hypotheses: `TauCeti.commutatorElement_transvectionUnit`, with `commute_transvectionUnit` for the non-chaining pairs. They assume A commutative, whereas the layer's ring A is arbitrary: the roadmap says 'commutative' where it needs it (U.3, Z.2, Z.3) and uses K₁ of division rings for the Dieudonné determinant. Missing: the identities over a noncommutative ring.

targets.target: Normality of E(A) in GL(A)
targets.note: Not stated at any rank. Tau Ceti has only conjugation formulas for transvections, by diagonal matrices (`diagGL_mul_transvectionUnit_mul_inv`), by Weyl elements (`transvectionWeylElement_mul_transvectionUnit_mul_inv_left` and its siblings) and under the inverse-transpose automorphism (`inverseTranspose_transvectionUnit`), together with a generator-level criterion for one closure to normalise another (`closure_le_normalizer_closure`).

targets.target: Perfectness of the elementary group
targets.note: Mathlib proves that SL(2,F) is perfect over a field with some a ≠ 0, a² ≠ 1 (`Matrix.SL2.commutator_eq_top`). Missing: perfectness of E_n(A) for n ≥ 3 over a ring, and of E(A).

targets.target: Whitehead's lemma [GL(A), GL(A)] = E(A)
targets.note: Tau Ceti has the key ingredient over any commutative ring: `diag2nUnit_decompose` writes diag(a, a⁻¹), for a unit a at two coordinates, as a product of six transvections, and the commutator relation makes every transvection a commutator in rank ≥ 3. The equality of the commutator subgroup with the elementary subgroup is not stated at any rank.

targets.target: Classical K₁(A) = GL(A)/E(A), compared with the abelianisation of GL(A)
targets.note: Neither library defines K₁ of a ring or the stable group GL(A): there is no colimit of the GL_n tower, no stable elementary subgroup and no quotient GL(A)/E(A). The abelianisation of GL_n(A) is not computed either.

targets.target: Functoriality for ring homomorphisms, block-sum multiplication, stabilisation invariance, trivial class of elementary matrices
targets.note: Only the matrix-level ingredients exist: `Matrix.GeneralLinearGroup.map` along a ring homomorphism, and Tau Ceti's `map_transvectionUnit`, which says transvections map to transvections. There is no K₁ to be functorial.

targets.target: K₁ class of an automorphism of a finite projective module via a projective complement, independent of the complement
targets.note: Complements exist: a finitely generated projective is a retract of Rⁿ (`Module.Finite.exists_comp_eq_id_of_projective`, `Module.Projective.iff_split`), but no K₁ class of an automorphism is defined.

targets.target: Additivity along a projective filtration, and compatibility with direct sums and scalar extension
targets.note: Absent with K₁. Only the determinant shadow exists over commutative rings: the determinant of a block sum is the product (`LinearMap.det_prodMap`) and determinants commute with base change (`LinearMap.det_baseChange`).

targets.target: Stable determinant K₁(A) → Aˣ for commutative A, with its section from Aˣ
targets.note: `Matrix.GeneralLinearGroup.det : GL n R →* Rˣ` exists at each finite rank and is surjective (`det_surjective`). The stable determinant on K₁ does not, since K₁ does not.

targets.target: SK₁(A) as the kernel of the determinant, and the split decomposition K₁(A) ≅ Aˣ ⊕ SK₁(A)
targets.note: Absent with K₁. At finite rank the kernel of the determinant is SL_n(A) (`Matrix.SpecialLinearGroup.range_toGL`).

targets.target: SK₁ vanishing for fields by explicit elementary reduction
targets.note: Tau Ceti proves the finite-rank statement in full: `closure_range_toSpecialLinearGroup_eq_top_of_field` says SL_ι(K) is generated by transvections for any field K and finite index type ι, that is SL_n(K) = E_n(K), by Mathlib's explicit reduction to a diagonal matrix (`SpecialLinearGroup.exists_list_transvec_mul_diagonal_mul_list_transvec`). Missing: the statement for SK₁ as a quotient of the stable group.

targets.target: SK₁ vanishing for commutative semilocal rings
targets.note: No elementary generation of SL_n over a local or semilocal ring is proved in either library; the Tau Ceti generation theorems cover only fields and ℤ.

targets.target: Dieudonné determinant for a division ring, valued in the abelianisation of its multiplicative group
targets.note: Mathlib has Dieudonné's generation theorem for GL of a finite-dimensional space over a division ring, in the non-exceptional case (`LinearEquiv.mem_transvections_pow_mul_dilatransvections_of_not_isExceptional`), but no Dieudonné determinant.

targets.target: Bass–Milnor–Serre: SK₁(O_{F,S}) = 0 for a number field F and finite S
targets.note: Only the case F = ℚ, S = ∅ is present, in every finite rank: Tau Ceti proves SL_n(ℤ) is generated by transvections by the Euclidean algorithm (`closure_range_toSpecialLinearGroup_eq_top`). Missing: every other number field, every nonempty S (already ℤ[1/p]), and the Bass–Milnor–Serre argument.

targets.target: Stable elementary generation via unimodular rows and Mennicke symbols, with the arithmetic norm/congruence arguments
targets.note: `grep -rn -i` for unimodular rows, Mennicke symbols, stable range and Bass–Milnor–Serre finds nothing relevant in either tree. The only trace is the length-two completion of a coprime pair to a column of an SL₂ matrix (`IsCoprime.exists_SL2_col`).

targets.target: K₁(O_{F,S}) ≅ O_{F,S}ˣ canonically via the determinant
targets.note: Absent with K₁.

targets.target: Dirichlet's S-unit theorem O_{F,S}ˣ ≅ μ(F) ⊕ ℤ^{r₁+r₂+|S|−1}
targets.note: The S = ∅ case is complete: Mathlib's unit theorem gives rank r₁+r₂−1 (`finrank_modTorsion`) and unique decomposition, and Tau Ceti packages it as (𝓞F)ˣ ≃* torsion × ℤ^rank. For finite S, Tau Ceti proves only that the S-units are finitely generated (`Set.unit_fg`, `Set.unit_fg_of_units`) and the left-exact sequence 1 → Rˣ → O_Sˣ → ℤ^S (`Set.unitValuation_ker`). Missing: the rank r₁+r₂+|S|−1.

targets.target: Finite-field and local-ring specialisations, and the unit inclusion into K₁(F)
targets.note: Absent with K₁.

targets.target: Congruence subgroups and relative elementary subgroups for a pair (A, I)
targets.note: Only ℤ-cases exist: Mathlib's `CongruenceSubgroup.Gamma N`, the kernel of SL(2,ℤ) → SL(2,ℤ/N), and Tau Ceti's splitting of SL_n(ℤ) into factors congruent to 1 modulo coprime moduli. Missing: GL_n(A, I) for a general ideal and the relative elementary subgroup E(A, I).

targets.target: Relative K₁(A, I) compared with the homotopy-fibre definition, not defined as ker(K₁(A) → K₁(A/I))
targets.note: Absent with K₁ and with any homotopy theory of K-theory spaces.

targets.target: The beginning of the relative exact sequence, with its K₂ boundary term made explicit
targets.note: Absent.

targets.target: Transfer along a finite projective algebra extension by restriction of scalars, agreeing with the field norm on units
targets.note: The matrix-level transfer exists for free extensions: restricting scalars of a linear map gives the block matrix of left-multiplication matrices (`LinearMap.restrictScalars_toMatrix`) with determinant the norm of the determinant (`LinearMap.det_restrictScalars`), and Tau Ceti's `unitsLeftMulMatrix : Sˣ →* GL_ι(R)` has determinant `Algebra.norm` (`val_det_unitsLeftMulMatrix`). Missing: the transfer on K₁ for a finite projective, not necessarily free, extension, and its agreement with the norm there.

targets.target: Projection formula against K₀, and the boundary Lˣ → K₀(residue field) of a discrete valuation field equal to the valuation
targets.note: No K₁, no transfer and no localisation boundary map.

duplicates.note: Defines relative K-theory of a pair (A, I) as the homotopy fibre of A → A/I, with its connecting homomorphisms: the definition and relative exact sequence that this layer's relative K₁ must match.
Applies the localisation sequence to a DVR and Dedekind domains and identifies the boundary on units with the valuation, which is this layer's boundary target.

targets.target: Identification of π₁ BGL(A)⁺ with GL(A)/E(A), matching determinant and transfer
targets.note: Neither library has the plus construction, a classifying space BGL(A) or a K-theory space; `grep -rn -i hurewicz` finds only a remark about Hurewicz fibrations.

targets.target: K₁ of ℤ, of finite fields, of ℤ[1/p] and of a product of fields
targets.note: Only the finite-rank inputs for ℤ and for fields exist: SL_n(ℤ) = E_n(ℤ) and SL_n(K) = E_n(K) (Tau Ceti), with the surjective determinant GL_n → units (Mathlib `Matrix.GeneralLinearGroup.det_surjective`). Missing: the K₁ groups themselves, ℤ[1/p] and products of fields.

targets.target: Test: a triangular matrix has the product of its diagonal units as determinant class
targets.note: The determinant of a triangular matrix is the product of its diagonal entries (`Matrix.det_of_isUpperTriangular`, and Tau Ceti's `Matrix.BlockTriangular.det_eq_prod_diag` for an injective block labelling). The statement about its K₁ class is missing.

targets.target: Test: diag(g, g⁻¹) has trivial class after stabilisation
targets.note: Tau Ceti's `diag2nUnit_decompose` proves the scalar case: diag(a, a⁻¹) for a unit a is a product of transvections, over any commutative ring. Missing: the block-matrix case diag(g, g⁻¹) for g ∈ GL_n(A), and the K₁ statement.

targets.target: Test: the valuation boundary of a uniformiser is 1
targets.note: The valuation side exists: a uniformiser of a DVR has additive valuation 1 (`IsDiscreteValuationRing.addVal_uniformizer`). Missing: the boundary map K₁(L) → K₀(k) and its identification with the valuation.

duplicates.note: Identifies the explicit K₁ model with the degree-one group of the K-theory space, the comparison this layer states as π₁BGL(A)⁺ ≅ GL(A)/E(A).
Its K_{2j−1}(F_q) ≅ ℤ/(q^j−1) at j = 1, with the recovery of the determinant in degree one, is this layer's K₁ of a finite field.
Computes the first four K-groups of ℤ, including this layer's K₁(ℤ).

targets.target: Finitely generated projectives are the direct summands of finite free modules, with the complement, splitting maps and idempotent available
targets.note: `Module.Finite.exists_comp_eq_id_of_projective` exhibits a finitely generated projective as a retract of Rⁿ, with f ∘ g = id, and `Module.Projective.of_split` gives the converse. The idempotent endomorphism g ∘ f of Rⁿ, which is the idempotent matrix, and `LinearMap.isProj_iff_isIdempotentElem` relating idempotents to projections, are available.

targets.target: Correspondence between idempotent matrices up to stabilised equivalence and isomorphism classes of finitely generated projectives
targets.note: Mathlib matches idempotent endomorphisms with complemented submodules (`Submodule.isIdempotentElemEquiv`), and Tau Ceti identifies Hom(Ae, Af) with the corner eAf (`spanSingletonHomEquivCorner`), but there is no classification of projectives by idempotent matrices up to stabilised conjugacy.

targets.target: Ring K₀ defined through the existing split/exact K₀ universal property
targets.note: Tau Ceti builds the exact category of finitely generated projective modules over any ring (`finiteProjectiveModulesExactStructure`, in `Algebra/Category/ModuleCat/CartanMap.lean`). Its exact K₀ carries the universal property for additive invariants (`ExactK0.liftEquiv`); `SplitK0.liftEquiv` is the split version.

targets.target: Object-class induction and equality of classes by stable isomorphism
targets.note: Every element is a difference [P] − [Q] (`SplitK0.exists_eq_sub`). The comparison with Mathlib's group completion of the monoid of isomorphism classes (`SplitK0.grothendieckAddGroupEquiv`) and Schanuel's lemma are present. Missing: the statement that [P] = [Q] exactly when P ⊕ Rⁿ ≅ Q ⊕ Rⁿ for some n, which would follow from the group-completion comparison and cofinality of free modules.

targets.target: Scalar extension and Morita functoriality of ring K₀
targets.note: The generic pieces exist: `SplitK0.map` and `mapEquiv` along additive functors and equivalences, base change preserving projectivity (`Module.Projective.tensorProduct`) and Mathlib's Morita equivalence, including R ~ Mₙ(R). Missing: the scalar-extension map on ring K₀ and Morita invariance of K₀.

targets.target: Direct-sum relations suffice, because every short exact sequence of projectives with projective quotient splits
targets.note: `finiteProjectiveModulesExactStructure_eq_split` proves that the exact structure on finitely generated projectives is the split one, and `ExactK0.fromSplitEquiv` identifies split and exact K₀ in that situation. The underlying facts are Mathlib's `LinearMap.exists_rightInverse_of_surjective` and `ShortComplex.ShortExact.splittingOfProjective`.

duplicates.note: Also constructs the exact category of finitely generated projectives with scalar extension, identifies π₀ with K₀(A), and proves that every finitely generated projective has a complement making it free.
Defines K₀(proj A) for a finite-dimensional algebra and proves its Morita invariance, the special case of this layer's Morita functoriality.
Proves Morita invariance of K-theory for rings, which in degree zero is this layer's Morita functoriality of ring K₀.

targets.target: Rank of a finitely generated projective over a commutative ring as a locally constant function on Spec A, constant on a connected spectrum
targets.note: `Module.rankAtStalk M : PrimeSpectrum R → ℕ` is locally constant for finitely presented flat modules (`isLocallyConstant_rankAtStalk`), which covers finitely generated projectives via `Module.Flat.of_projective` and `Module.finitePresentation_of_projective`. On a connected spectrum it is constant by `IsLocallyConstant.apply_eq_of_preconnectedSpace`. It is ℕ-valued, which is the stated integer rank.

targets.target: Finite image of the rank function and compatibility with localisation and base change
targets.note: Finite image: `IsLocallyConstant.range_finite` on the compact space Spec A. Base change is `Module.rankAtStalk_baseChange`, and more generally `rankAtStalk_isBaseChange`. Localisation is the base change along A → S⁻¹A (`LocalizedModule.isBaseChange`). Mathlib also has multiplicativity under tensor products.

targets.target: K₀(F) ≅ ℤ for fields and division rings, by dimension
targets.note: `TauCeti.SplitK0.finrankEquiv : SplitK0 (FGModuleCat k) ≃+ ℤ` for any division ring k, sending a class to its dimension, and the abelian version `AbelianK0.finrankEquiv`. It is stated on the category of finite-dimensional k-modules. Over a division ring this is the category of finitely generated projectives, so the transport to `finiteProjectiveModulesExactStructure k` is formal (`SplitK0.mapEquiv` with `ExactK0.fromSplitEquiv`), though not stated; `cartanEquivOfIsSemisimpleRing` gives a second route.

targets.target: Finite-product formula for K₀, and the test K₀(F × F) ≅ ℤ²
targets.note: No product formula K₀(A × B) ≅ K₀(A) ⊕ K₀(B) is stated; its rank shadow is `Module.rankAtStalk_prod` and `rankAtStalk_pi`. The test case is within reach for semisimple rings such as F × F: Tau Ceti proves K₀(proj R) ≃ G₀(mod R) (`cartanEquivOfIsSemisimpleRing`) and gives G₀ of an Artinian ring the basis of classes of an exhaustive family of pairwise nonisomorphic simple modules (`simpleClassBasis`). Missing: the general product formula and the stated computation K₀(F × F) ≅ ℤ², which needs the two simple modules exhibited.

targets.target: Finitely generated projectives over a local ring are free
targets.note: `Module.free_of_flat_of_isLocalRing` shows that a finite flat module over a commutative local ring is free, the setting of this rank paragraph. With `Module.Flat.of_projective` this is more general than the layer's Nakayama and finite-presentation route.

targets.target: The semilocal decomposition, stated with its connected-component information
targets.note: Mathlib proves that over a ring with finitely many maximal ideals, a finite flat module of constant rank at the maximal ideals is free (`Module.free_of_flat_of_finrank_eq`, Stacks 02M9), and Tau Ceti splits a ring whose spectrum has finitely many connected components as the product over the components (`PrimeSpectrum.ringEquivPiQuotientConnectedComponentsIdeal`). Missing: the decomposition of K₀ of a semilocal ring by connected components.

duplicates.note: States K₀(F_q) = ℤ, the finite-field case of this layer's K₀(F) ≅ ℤ for fields.
Proves finite-product compatibility of K-theory for rings, which in degree zero is this layer's finite-product formula K₀(A × B) ≅ K₀(A) ⊕ K₀(B).

targets.target: The ring structure on K₀ of a commutative ring from the tensor product
targets.note: Tau Ceti gives `SplitK0 C` a commutative ring structure, with [X]·[Y] = [X ⊗ Y], for any braided monoidal preadditive category with biproducts (`SplitK0.instCommRing`). Missing: the monoidal structure on finitely generated projective modules that would give ring K₀ this multiplication.

targets.target: Exterior powers of finite projectives and the filtration formula for an extension
targets.note: Mathlib defines ⋀[R]^n M for every module, with freeness and the rank formula (n choose k) for free modules, and the exterior algebra of a product. Missing: projectivity of ⋀ⁿ of a finitely generated projective, and the filtration of ⋀ⁿ M for 0 → M' → M → M'' → 0.

targets.target: λ-ring identities on K₀, extended from modules to virtual classes
targets.note: There is no λ-ring, γ-operation or Adams operation in either library. `BinomialRing` exists, and Mathlib's docstrings (`Binomial.lean`, `Dickson.lean`) record that λ-rings are not formalised.

targets.target: The determinant of a projective of locally constant rank, defined componentwise, compared with Pic
targets.note: Only the free case exists: for a module with a basis of size n, Tau Ceti identifies ⋀ⁿM with R (`exteriorPower.topEquiv`) and shows endomorphisms act on it by det. Mathlib proves that a stably free invertible module is free. Missing: the top exterior power of a projective of locally constant rank as an invertible module.

targets.target: Determinant as an additive homomorphism K₀(A) → Pic(A), with tensor product as the Picard operation
targets.note: The target `CommRing.Pic`, the group of invertible modules under tensor product, exists; the determinant map on K₀ does not.

targets.target: The augmentation (rank) kernel and its relation with the γ-filtration; degree-zero normalisation of the Adams operations
targets.note: No γ-filtration and no Adams operations in either library.

duplicates.note: Compares the external product with tensor products on K₀, the same K₀ ring structure this layer constructs.
Constructs λ-operations and Adams operations on K-theory, whose degree-zero part is this layer's λ-ring structure on K₀.
Constructs the γ-filtration, which this layer relates to the rank kernel.

targets.target: Steinitz classification: a positive-rank finite projective over a Dedekind domain is free plus an invertible ideal
targets.note: Only rank one is present: Mathlib proves that an invertible module is isomorphic to an ideal whenever the Picard group of the fraction ring is trivial, in particular over a domain (`Module.Invertible.exists_linearEquiv_ideal`). Missing: the decomposition in rank ≥ 2. Mathlib's Dedekind-domain module theory otherwise covers torsion modules and 'flat iff torsion-free'.

targets.target: I ⊕ J ≅ A ⊕ IJ for invertible ideals
targets.note: Not stated in either library.

targets.target: (rank, det): K₀(A) ≅ ℤ ⊕ Pic(A) for a Dedekind domain, with its inverse, independence of ideal representatives, and the zero module separately
targets.note: Both components of the target exist (`CommRing.Pic`, `Module.rankAtStalk`), but neither the determinant map nor the isomorphism does.

targets.target: Comparison of Pic with the existing ideal class group
targets.note: `ClassGroup.equivPic : ClassGroup R ≃* Pic R` holds for every domain, which is more general than the Dedekind case.

targets.target: Specialisation to O_F and O_{F,S}: the class group of the S-integers is the class group modulo the classes of the primes in S
targets.note: Tau Ceti proves Cl(𝒪_S) ≃* Cl(R)/⟨[v] : v ∈ S⟩ for any Dedekind domain R (`IsDedekindDomain.integerClassGroupEquiv`). There 𝒪_S is the valuation-defined overring `Set.integer`, which the docstring of Tau Ceti's `SInteger/Basic.lean` notes is not in general a localisation. Missing: the K₀ statement, and the identification with the localised ring the layer names.

targets.target: Induced maps under localisation, extension of number fields and finite flat restriction of scalars; transfer of an ideal class by the determinant/norm formula
targets.note: The Pic-level maps exist: Pic is functorial along any algebra, localisation included (`CommRing.Pic.mapAlgebra`); extension of ideal classes (`ClassGroup.extendedHom`), which onto the S-integers is surjective with kernel generated by the classes of S (`IsDedekindDomain.ker_integer_extendedHom`); and the relative norm on class groups, with norm ∘ extension = [L:K]-th power (`ClassGroup.relNorm`, `relNorm_extendedHom`, packaged as `ClassGroup.extendedRelNormHom`). Missing: the maps on K₀ and the transfer's determinant formula.

duplicates.note: States K₀(O_{F,S}) ≅ ℤ ⊕ Cl(O_{F,S}) and compares norms and extension of ideals with K-theory transfer and pullback, restating this layer's specialisation to O_{F,S} and its induced maps, although this roadmap's document names N.1 as their consumer.
Derives the ideal-class-group sequence from the localisation sequence, i.e. the localisation map K₀(O_F) → K₀(O_{F,S}) and the quotient of the class group by the primes in S described here.

targets.target: K₀ of finite locally free sheaves on a scheme, from the categorical construction
targets.note: `SheafOfModules.IsLocallyFree` exists, but no exact category of vector bundles and no K₀ of a scheme.

targets.target: K₀(X) ≅ ℤ ⊕ Pic(X) by rank and determinant, for a connected regular noetherian curve
targets.note: Absent. Tau Ceti's `LineBundleClass X` is only a commutative monoid of isomorphism classes of invertible sheaves, with inverses deliberately not provided, so there is no Pic(X) group to map to.

targets.target: Structure-sheaf and skyscraper-sheaf class formulas through the K/G comparison, so that a divisor class agrees with a line-bundle class
targets.note: Tau Ceti maps Weil divisor classes to line-bundle classes additively and injectively on integral noetherian schemes of dimension ≤ 1 whose codimension-one local rings are DVRs (`classGroupToLineBundleClass_injective`, `classGroupToLineBundleClassHom`). Surjectivity is not proved. The K-theoretic class formulas need K₀ and G₀ of the curve, which are missing.

targets.target: Pic(E) ≅ ℤ ⊕ E(F) for an elliptic curve with rational origin, hence K₀(E) ≅ ℤ² ⊕ E(F); not for genus-one curves without a rational point
targets.note: Tau Ceti has both halves at the level of function-field divisor classes. E(F) is the degree-zero class group (`pointEquivDegreeZeroDivisorClass`, via `Point.toClassEquiv`, assuming the coordinate ring is Dedekind, which Tau Ceti proves for elliptic curves), degree-one places of a genus-one function field form the degree-zero class group (`Place.degreeOneAddEquivDegreeZeroClassGroup`), and a class group with a degree-one point splits as Pic⁰ × ℤ (`OrderSystem.classGroupAddEquivPicZeroProdInt`; `ker_degreeClass_eq_picZero` identifies the function-field Pic⁰). Missing: the scheme-level Picard group of E and the K₀ consequence.

duplicates.note: Also proves the Picard decomposition Pic(E) ≅ ℤ ⊕ E(F) on an elliptic curve with rational origin and K₀(E) ≅ ℤ² ⊕ E(F).
Owns the Weil/Cartier/line-bundle dictionary Cl(X) ≅ Pic X on a smooth curve and its degree, the divisor-class/line-bundle agreement this layer uses.

targets.target: Agreement of these definitions and maps with π₀ of the general K-theory
targets.note: No higher K-theory space or spectrum exists in either library, so there is no π₀K to compare with.

targets.target: Localisation sends a projective class to its localised class and a perfect complex to its Euler class
targets.note: No K₀ localisation map and no perfect complexes of modules. The nearest constructions are Tau Ceti's alternating class in K₀(proj R) of a module with a finite projective resolution (`moduleEulerClassOf`) and the Euler class of bounded complexes in abelian K₀ (`AbelianK0.eulerChar`).

targets.target: Comparison of the Cartan map K₀ → G₀ with the existing general Cartan map
targets.note: The existing general Cartan map is Tau Ceti's `TauCeti.cartanMap : K₀(proj R) →+ G₀(mod R)` for any ring. It is an isomorphism when every finitely generated module has a finite projective resolution (`cartanEquiv`). Any ring K₀ built on `finiteProjectiveModulesExactStructure` uses it directly. Missing: the scheme-level Cartan map and the comparison of the layer's degree-zero maps with it.

targets.target: Tests: fields, ℤ, a product of two fields, and a Dedekind domain with a nonprincipal ideal class
targets.note: K₀ of a field or division ring is computed (`SplitK0.finrankEquiv`), and K₀ of a semisimple ring such as F × F reduces to G₀ (`cartanEquivOfIsSemisimpleRing`). For ℤ only the input exists (finitely generated torsion-free modules over a PID are free, `Module.free_of_finite_type_torsion_free'`), and a nonprincipal ideal class is available in ℚ(√−5), whose class number is 2 (`classNumber_adjoinRoot_sqrt_neg_five_eq_two`). Missing: the stated K₀(ℤ) and K₀(F × F) computations and the nonprincipal-ideal test, which needs K₀ ≅ ℤ ⊕ Pic.

targets.target: K₀(P¹_F) ≅ ℤ² by the projective-bundle construction and by rank/Pic, with the two bases compared
targets.note: No projective-bundle formula and no K₀ of a scheme in either library.

duplicates.note: Identifies the components of the K-theory space of A with K₀(A): the same agreement of ring K₀ with π₀K.
Proves the projective-bundle theorem and compares it with this layer's P¹ calculation, i.e. K₀(P¹_F) ≅ ℤ².
Computes the K-theory of P¹ by the projective-bundle theorem, including this layer's K₀(P¹_F) ≅ ℤ² test.
Computes the first four K-groups of ℤ, including this layer's K₀(ℤ) test.

Constructs the Cartan map K(X) → G(X), with the affine comparisons, and proves it an equivalence for regular noetherian schemes: the same K₀ → G₀ Cartan comparison this layer must make against the existing map.
